summary:
Responding to the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge "Abandoned but Not Forgotten," we developed an educational game.

We know that children and adults alike love games, and collection-and-reward games are especially popular today. So we decided to use this popular game format to bring knowledge and education into entertainment.

In Space Nexus, players explore the Moon, collect historical objects, and bring them to a base. However, collecting an object is not enough to earn a reward. Players must correctly answer a quiz question about the collected object to receive points.

The game also introduces each historical object and tells its story in an engaging, interactive, and exciting way, allowing players to discover objects they may never have heard of before.

Instead of relying solely on complex technical manuals or scientific books, Space Nexus makes the history of space exploration more accessible and enjoyable for people of all ages.

Our goal is to transform entertainment into a learning experience, spark curiosity about science, and, who knows, inspire the next generation of scientists.
details:
Project Details – Space Nexus

Space Nexus is an educational game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, inspired by the challenge "Abandoned but Not Forgotten."

Our original idea was to use something that children and young people already love: games. Collection and reward games have become extremely popular, so we decided to use this excitement to bring players closer to science and space exploration.

In Space Nexus, players explore a lunar environment, search for historical objects left behind during space missions, collect them, and return them to a base. To earn rewards, players must correctly answer quiz questions about the collected objects. They also discover additional information about each object's history and importance to space exploration.

Our goal is to show that, long before today's advanced technology, humanity had already developed the knowledge and technology needed to explore space. Many of these historical objects have fascinating stories that people may never have heard before.

The creative aspect of Space Nexus is transforming a popular gaming experience into an opportunity for scientific discovery. Instead of simply reading complex scientific books or technical documents, players can learn about space exploration through an interactive, accessible, and exciting experience.

To develop the game, we used GDevelop, a game development platform with visual programming, 3D game creation features, and integrated artificial intelligence tools. Its resources helped us build the lunar environment, develop game mechanics, implement interactive quizzes, and test and improve the gameplay.

We also used ChatGPT to support brainstorming, organize ideas, improve texts, translate content into English, and assist with technical problem-solving. For our presentation video, we used CapCut, including its text-to-speech technology to generate English narration.

Historical information, scientific descriptions, and quiz content were based on NASA educational resources and materials. NASA images and references also helped us represent the objects and their historical context.

Throughout development, we considered the interests of younger generations, accessibility for different age groups, the importance of scientific accuracy, and the challenge of combining entertainment with meaningful learning.

This first version focuses on the Moon, but we hope to continue developing and improving Space Nexus in the future, expanding its content, enhancing the gameplay, and introducing new opportunities for scientific discovery.

Our greatest ambition is to reach more and more children and young people, awakening their curiosity about science, technology, and space exploration.

We believe that future scientists may already be among the millions of young people who love playing games. Perhaps we just need to bring science to where they already are.

Space Nexus is our attempt to turn entertainment into curiosity, curiosity into knowledge, and knowledge into inspiration for the next generation of scientists.
